result.title: Agent Evaluation Without Ground Truth: A Null Proportion Perspective
result.summary: The correctness of actions taken by agents is typically evaluated against known, externally verified ground truth labels, such as whether a proof is correct or whether code compiles and passes unit tests. However, as coding and science agents are entrusted with more end-to-end autonomy -- proposing interventions, running experiments, and deciding what to deploy and investigate next -- whether an agent's actions genuinely improve an outcome must be inferred from noisy, often inconclusive experiments. To evaluate agents in this setting, we define agent quality as a weighted sum of correct decisions along its trajectory, using sequences of $e$-values as statistical evidence regarding correctness in place of ground-truth labels. Our framework accommodates arbitrarily dependent decisions, data-dependent trajectory termination, dynamically generated hypotheses, and quality measures defined after the trajectory concludes. We construct upper and lower bound estimators and confidence sets for agent quality with statistical guarantees that hold uniformly over agent trajectory distributions and establish instance-wise sharpness of our estimator class. We demonstrate our methods with a case study comparing the success of Claude Opus and Claude Haiku in improving the runtime of an open-source Python package.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究无外部 ground truth 时的 agent 质量评估：用 e-values 序列替代标签作为正确性统计证据，将质量定义为轨迹上正确决策的加权和，构造上下界估计与置信集，并在 Claude Opus 与 Haiku 改进 Python 包运行时的案例中演示。
AI.relevance_reason: 其轨迹级决策质量的统计估计与置信集，可能为 LVR 中缺少标签的推理步评价、停止决策与轨迹贡献分配提供可核查的方法线索，但 e-value 假设能否对应 latent 推理步骤尚需阅读正文确认。
